summary: Tiletum is a dense modern Euro where each turn you place a die-worker on the board to gather resources, artisans, or favors, then spend a busy engine of contracts, cathedral construction, and noble alliances to convert everything into points. It plays like a checklist optimization puzzle more than a story, with heavy AP-prone decision points and a strong sense of an engine coming together over the course of the game.
praised: satisfying engine-building and multiple viable strategies
high production values and thematic Renaissance dressing
rewarding for players who like Luciani/Tascini-style resource conversion puzzles
criticised: heavy analysis paralysis, especially in 4-player games
dense iconography and rules overhead for new players
can feel more like a solitaire optimization exercise than an interactive game
randomness in die results some find frustrating at this weight

interaction.kind: shared board space drafting with mostly parallel tableau-building
interaction.detail: Players compete for the same limited spaces on shared tracks and the fair/market area, so timing and blocking matter, but each player mostly develops their own private engine of contracts and buildings. Direct conflict is minimal; interaction is mostly about racing for the same resource nodes.

scoring.how_you_win: Accumulate the most VP across several parallel engines (contracts, cathedrals, coats of arms, favor/notable people) over a fixed number of rounds; most total prestige wins.
